messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT fired: GPU_MEM_SATURATION on pool: inference-west2a (trigger: > 92% for 60s). Sampled hosts: gpu-ww-12, gpu-ww-15. PagerDuty incident PD-9876 created.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: PD-9876 triggered (High). Assigned: oncall@redwood-eng. Escalation policy: eng-oncall -> eng-oncall-2.

maria: acked. I'm on it, grabbing logs and checking pool autoscale.

ashok: thx. ping me if it looks like a kernel or mem leak. I'll watch alloc errors.

maria: quick summary from metrics: memory utilization jumped from ~60% to 95% across the pool over ~90s, sustained. Per-host spike on gpu-ww-15 correlates with heavy kvcache churn. No immediate driver resets in metrics.

maria: running: `ssh ops@gpu-ww-15 sudo journalctl -u inference-runtime -n 200 --no-pager | sed -n '1,120p'`

maria: logs (excerpt):
```
2026-03-15T18:53:21Z inference-runtime[3421]: model_shard.cpp:412 allocate_kv_cache() failed: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation: out of memory
2026-03-15T18:53:21Z inference-runtime[3421]: attention_kv.cc:87 KV cache resize fallback to host memory
2026-03-15T18:53:22Z inference-runtime[3421]: runtime: OOM backpressure triggered, dropping low-priority requests
```

ashok: that cudaErrorMemoryAllocation line is not great. Can you check if any long-running requests / huge seq-len traces are pinned? `redwoodctl requests list --host gpu-ww-15 --status running`

maria: found two heavy requests from customer app-api-99 with seq_len ~65k tokens (probing). I'm killing them now: `redwoodctl request cancel <reqid1>` and `<reqid2>`

maria: canceled. memory dropped to ~78% on gpu-ww-15. overall pool 85%. Still seeing kvcache thrash on logs.

ashok: good mitigation. can we temporarily lower max_seq_len per-tenant or enforce streaming chunking? If not, we should shed those tenants to Dedicated.

jules: customer-impact note: app-api-99 reported 5xxs for ~2m (estimated 120 failed requests). They are ondedicated? no, hosted. Ticket #CS-332 assigned to AE.

maria: placing routing override: routing-policy set inference-west2a -> fallback-small-llama for customers flagged as noisy. Command: `redwoodctl routing set --pool inference-west2a --policy "fallback_on_mem" --targets fallback-small-llama` (will apply in ~30s).

incident-bot: Escalation timer: if not acked by second oncall in 3m, auto-escalate. (Currently acked by maria).

ashok: monitoring eviction/reclaim counters: `nvtop` shows GPU memory stable after cancels. I'm watching for cuda driver messages: `dmesg | grep -i cuda` -> none. Good.

maria: added a soft limit for kvcache per-model: 2GB. Pushed config: `/etc/redwood/runtime/config.d/99-kvcache-softlimit.yaml` (rolled to gpu-ww-*)

maria: autoscale policy bumped min capacity +1 for inference-west2a to give breathing room: `redwoodctl pools update inference-west2a --min-instances 6`

jules: leaving note for follow-up: run a replay of app-api-99 request patterns in staging with kvcache saturation tests. Also consider adding a tenant-level seq_len quota.

ashok: agreed. follow-ups: (1) add tenant_seq_len guard + reject with 400; (2) investigate whether kvcache fragmentation causes host-local OOMs; (3) add clearer alert: "gpu mem saturation with cuda alloc errors" to reduce finger-pointing.

maria: pagerduty PD-9876: acknowledged -> resolved (manual mitigation + scale + cancel heavy reqs). Marking incident status: mitigated.

pagerduty: PD-9876 status changed to RESOLVED by maria. Duration: ~7m.

jules: assigning post-incident: ashok to own root-cause (kvcache fragmentation + tenant seq-len controls). maria to document mitigations & runbook updates. I'll draft customer comm for app-api-99.

maria: adding runbook entry: "GPU mem saturation — cancel heavy seq requests, apply kvcache softlimit, bump min replicas, route noisy tenants to fallback models." Pushing PR: https://git.redwood.ai/runs/PR-4721 :thumbsup:

ashok: leaving debug snippet in ticket: how to find offending requests + example `redwoodctl` commands.

incident-bot: Note: no driver resets, no host reboots. No further escalation required.

maria: closing thread. If anyone sees reoccurence, re-open PD or @pagerduty. :white_check_mark:
